status: Wave 3 world slice 1: 3D block field, mountains, caves, danger rings

map.design_purpose: Bounded sandpit dimensions and terrain character (D-003, grown for the Wave 3 world pass). world_depth is the vertical block budget: y=0 bedrock, surface rolls around base_height + noise*height_scale, mountains climb from there and caves wind below. 160x160 at 1 m keeps the world bounded but far enough out that leaving the heartland is a journey.

mountains.design_purpose: The verticality layer: where the slow cragginess field exceeds its threshold, ridged noise piles up to extra_scale further blocks - localized massifs with cliffs and vistas instead of uniformly lumpy ground. Raising the threshold makes mountains rarer; raising extra_scale makes them taller.

strata.design_purpose: Blocks under the biome surface block: dirt_depth of dirt, then stone to bedrock. What a cliff face or cave wall shows, and (come the digging slice) what shovelling yields before the pick is needed.

caves.design_purpose: Carved cave systems: two intersecting 3D noise level-sets (tunnel_width sets how fat the intersection is) wind spaghetti tunnels; a third field above cavern_threshold opens caverns in the lower cavern_max_y_fraction of a column. Tunnels normally keep surface_margin blocks of roof, but breach_chance of columns may carve through the top - natural entrances you can find and drop into. node_density seeds cave floors with nodes: iron runs richer underground, which is the reason to go down before digging exists. packs den Gloom Crawlers on the same floors - the dark is inhabited. The spawn clearing and gate ground are never carved.

danger.design_purpose: Danger scales with distance from spawn: the first ring containing a cell multiplies pack density, appends pack_size_bonus extra members drawn from the pack's own kind, and rolls elite_chance for one member to carry an elite modifier (world.json elite_modifiers). The heartland stays learnable and elite-free; the far rings are where packs grow teeth and the elite bounties live.

block_rules.design_purpose: Breaking generic terrain blocks (owner ask, 2 Sep 2026): hold LMB on a block to dig it out. The mechanic's cost is time - dig_seconds per kind, stone slower than soil - with tool tiers deferred until crafting wants them. Soil (surface turf, dirt) yields nothing yet because no soil material family exists; digging soil buys ACCESS (mine down, open a cave, cut a pit the horde falls into). Stone yields the stone family, so rock faces are a real quarry beside boulders. Bedrock at y 0 is the world's floor and never breaks.

biomes.design_purpose: High ground owns stone and iron; Stone Husks make taking them feel like a claim, and the climb telegraphs risk. height_min tracks base_height + 7 so the biome sits on genuinely raised ground
The dangerous quarter that holds the trial gate: fire creatures preview the Tyrant's element and the ground itself looks burnt; shrieker packs recruit the wastes against you
Wood country: dense trees with hound packs prowling, so bulk timber runs stay tense; a shrieker among the hounds turns a timber run into a hunt
The gentle fallback biome and starting country: sparse resources, near-empty of threats, readable in every direction

nodes.design_purpose: What each scattered node yields per E-press and how much it holds before depleting; visual keys pick the greybox mesh/texture. Cave-floor nodes use the same types (caves.node_density decides which). era (default 1) is the era a node type surfaces in (eras.json, D-019): the world map places every node from the seed, and the engine reveals the ones whose era has come - copper and tin glint on the cave floors once the deep wakes.

guarantees.design_purpose: D-003 authored-content rules: every valid seed starts in a safe flat meadow clearing (never carved beneath), has enough wood/stone/iron within a short walk to reach the forge, keeps mob packs off the doorstep, and places the trial gate far away in the wastes so it is an ambition before it is a destination. gate_min_distance grew with the map
